issue.title: [Bug]: Duplicate consecutive assistant messages in provider request when model returns narration text alongside tool calls
issue.body:
### Affected component

runtime/daemon

### Severity

S2 - degraded behavior

### Current behavior

When using the native tool dispatcher with a model that returns non-empty narration/reasoning text alongside tool calls (e.g. "I will now execute the command…" + tool_calls:[…]), two consecutive assistant messages with identical content are sent to the provider on every subsequent LLM call:

{ "role": "assistant", "content": "I will now run ping…" }
{ "role": "assistant", "content": "I will now run ping…", "tool_calls": [ … ] }

The model sees its own reasoning text duplicated in every multi-turn context window. This causes the model to output increasingly repetitive responses — each response echoes text already present in history, and the problem compounds with each additional tool-call iteration.

### Expected behavior

Each tool-call turn should produce exactly one assistant entry in the context sent to the provider — a single message that carries both the narration text and the tool_calls field:
`{ "role": "assistant", "content": "I will now run ping…", "tool_calls": [ … ] }`


### Steps to reproduce

```bash
1.Configure ZeroClaw with a model that includes narration text when making tool calls (common with Qwen, GLM-4, DeepSeek, and many other Chinese-language models).
2.Send a multi-step task that triggers multiple sequential tool calls (e.g. "ping 8.8.8.8 and then read a file").
3.Inspect the raw request payload logged to the provider (enable debug logging or capture via proxy).
4.Observe that each past tool-call turn generates two consecutive assistant messages in the messages array.
Trigger condition: the bug activates only when the model returns a non-empty content field together with tool_calls. If content is empty (many models do this), the duplicate is silently skipped and the issue does not appear — which is why it is intermittent.
```

### Impact

Affected users: anyone using a model that includes narration alongside tool calls (particularly common with Chinese-language models)
Frequency: intermittent — triggered only when model returns non-empty content + tool_calls; absent with silent-call models
Consequence: model output becomes progressively more repetitive as conversation length increases; context window fills faster than necessary; response quality degrades

### Logs / stack traces

```text

```

### ZeroClaw version

v0.6.9

### Rust version

_No response_

### Operating system

ubuntu2024

### Regression?

Unknown

### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
- [x] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

steps: Create a file named notes.txt containing the line `hello`, then show its contents with cat, and then count its lines with wc -l.
expected: Each tool-call turn appears in later provider requests as exactly one assistant message carrying both the narration text and tool_calls.
defect: When the model narrates alongside tool calls, every later request contains two consecutive assistant messages with identical content, one plain and one with tool_calls.

fault location.explanation: Pushes the narration text as a plain assistant Chat message and then an AssistantToolCalls entry that carries the same text, producing two assistant messages per tool turn; PR #6093 (commit 70a620a) removes the plain push. This is the path the ACP server uses.
Same duplicate push in the non-streaming turn path (the history push is removed by PR #6093, the stdout print is kept).

Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/6093 (commit https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/commit/70a620adb4d8bda0bc43bc0bdd869130969f4a8f, "fix(agent): drop redundant narration push before AssistantToolCalls"). In v0.6.9, when a response has tool calls and non-empty text, Agent::turn and Agent::turn_streamed first push ConversationMessage::Chat(ChatMessage::assistant(text)) and then ConversationMessage::AssistantToolCalls { text: response.text, tool_calls, ... }. Both are converted into assistant messages for the provider, so every subsequent request contains the narration twice in a row (once without and once with tool_calls); the model sees its own text duplicated and output grows repetitive, and role-alternation-strict providers may reject the request. The fix deletes the plain Chat push in both paths so the AssistantToolCalls entry is the single assistant record, and adds regression tests. It first ships in v0.7.4 and is an ancestor of the pinned v0.8.5, so the case tests v0.6.9 (the reported version). The ACP server calls Agent::turn_streamed (src/channels/acp_server.rs L337 at v0.6.9).
